method: Independent frozen-source comparison, existing diagnostic/canonical result inspection and actual saved Figma411:94827 screenshot inspection. No new browser runs or source edits.
summary: Keep MS02–05 as P2 Modules source defects, scoped to the exact routes. Split MS06 functional join-link omission from its separate visual implementation gap. None demonstrates a canonical /calendar regression or authorization bypass. Normalize PROS-F01 to P2 alongside OWI-F01.

findings.reason: The shared architecture promises preserved verified-client selection. Modules useCalendar initializes its own clientId to an empty string and consequently queries unscoped accessible meetings even when the URL client was verified. This is incorrect scope presentation/selection, not a deliberately unavailable selector.
findings.canonicalComparison: Portfolio CalendarPage.tsx:49 consumes the URL clientId; :63–68 preserves other query fields on changes; :132–147 renders the selected scope. Canonical evidence passes scoped client/date/zone/view retention.
findings.action: Initialize and synchronize the Modules calendar scope from the verified selected-client boundary, then keep its selector and URL consistent. Preserve view/date when changing scope.
findings.rowImpact: Primarily the MCAL-003 scope-retention facet and Modules scope entry. MCAL-002 selector population itself is present; do not mark that entire criterion broken.
findings.limit: No evidence of widened backend permission. Master view still receives only the backend's accessible records.

findings.reason: MCAL-009 explicitly requires scheduled and due dates. Modules plannerItems uses dueOn ?? startOn and one task key, dropping a distinct start occurrence that the same available data can represent. No missing backend capability is needed to fix this.
findings.canonicalComparison: Portfolio plannerCalendarItems independently projects start and due with distinct keys, suppressing only an identical same-time occurrence. The supplied canonical diagnostic passes both dates with meetings denied.
findings.action: Project independently scheduled starts and dues, retain date/time precision, and deduplicate only genuinely identical occurrences.
findings.rowImpact: A Modules implementation failure of the scheduled/due facet. Keep the existing canonical /calendar MCAL-009 result intact.
findings.limit: Call this a confirmed source omission, not a temporal regression: this review did not establish an earlier good Modules revision.

findings.reason: CalendarEvents places the entire mixed Agenda under StatusPanel(meetings.error). StatusPanel returns early on a meetings error, so successfully loaded independent Planner items are hidden while their source counter remains. This breaks implemented composition and is not a planned unavailable source.
findings.canonicalComparison: Portfolio CalendarPage.tsx:70–75 combines successful feeds independently; :251–272 renders per-feed errors; :279–286 still renders available items. The canonical diagnostic confirms Planner survives denied meetings.
findings.action: Render each source's loading/error state independently of the mixed available Agenda; a denied meetings source must not suppress a successful Planner source.
findings.rowImpact: Modules mixed-source availability facet related to MCAL-013. It does not demonstrate permission widening or invalidate canonical source-isolation acceptance.
findings.limit: No authorization bypass claim; the failure is loss of independently authorized visible content.

findings.reason: The Agenda deliberately constructs a record-specific task link, but PlannerScreen never consumes its task parameter and TaskWorkspace initializes task to null. A user activating that link lands on generic My tasks. The task list/editor exist; the missing piece is the route-to-record binding.
findings.canonicalComparison: Canonical Portfolio Agenda does not create an equivalent internal Planner task link; plannerCalendarItems emits sourceId but no href and Agenda renders the task title as text. Therefore this is not a regression of canonical global-calendar navigation.
findings.action: Either implement current-authorized record resolution and open the selected task from this parameter, or remove the successful-looking record link until that binding exists. Prefer the former because the current UI already offers drilldown.
findings.rowImpact: Track as a distinct shipped Modules navigation defect. MCAL-009's literal criterion is task/date display, so do not use this alone to fail its date facet.
findings.limit: No claim that Planner writing or task access is generally unavailable. No earlier good Modules route version was demonstrated.

findings.functionalFinding: The reviewed engagement schema retains joinLink, but shared Meetings MeetingDetail never consumes it. A safe supplied join link should be usable in the existing detail surface. This is an actionable source omission independent of paid generation or service integration.
findings.visualFinding: Actual Figma411:94827 shows a list/detail split view, attendee line, Join and prep panel; the current Modules surface is a table plus modal. Record that as a distinct unimplemented design/presentation criterion, not a runtime regression. Do not bundle missing Meri generation with the join-link fix.
findings.canonicalComparison: Portfolio MeetingDetail.tsx:97–106 safely renders Join and :110–120 renders attendees. It uses a drawer, so canonical functional support does not establish that it matches the Modules split-view design.
findings.action: First surface the safe current join URL in Modules detail. Keep the list/detail visual rebuild and attendee projection as separately bounded acceptance work; keep Meri generation explicitly disabled until its contract is available.
findings.rowImpact: The omitted join link directly affects Modules' MCAL-006-equivalent functional facet. Layout mismatch belongs to Figma411:94827 visual acceptance. Do not reopen the canonical /calendar Join/attendee facet without separate evidence.
findings.limit: Attendee availability in the Modules response was not independently established here; the current Modules schema does not declare attendees. Do not claim that attendee rendering needs no contract review.

severityConsistency.recommendation: Normalize PROS-F01 from P1 to P2; retain OWI-F01 at P2.
severityConsistency.reason: Both show previously delivered cached records after a fresh list403. Objectives additionally opens an editor with old fields; Prospects opens a cached Pipeline. My prospect reproduction did not establish higher-impact exposure, another identity/tenant receiving data, a successful protected write, or server authorization bypass.
severityConsistency.impact: They still block current-access frontend acceptance for their respective surfaces and deserve a shared fix pattern: successful current read gating for records and dependent controls.
severityConsistency.originalEvidencePreserved: Original findings.json and report.md retain the initial P1 for audit traceability; this secondary recommendation supersedes that severity for root integration.
severityConsistency.unrelatedDataLoss: PROS-F02 is distinct: valid successful draft-save receipts trigger loss of text typed during the pending save. This severity review does not downgrade that finding.

testEvidenceLimit: Existing Modules diagnostic results:12 expected/0 unexpected. Canonical comparison:2 expected/0 unexpected. I inspected their result records and the corresponding source; I did not repeat those runs.
